The Cloudways Linode 2025 incident is an isolated outlier, not a pattern: across the first half of 2026 the plan returned to 99.99% uptime with just 35 minutes of downtime over 4 outages. Load Handling Under a 0-to-100 concurrent-user ramp, Cloudways Linode returned the fastest average for completed requests at 269 ms, followed by Cloudways Vultr at 279 ms and Cloudways Vultr HF at 288 ms. All three dropped a share of requests as the test approached peak load — Linode timed out on 2.2%, Vultr on 1.5%, and Vultr HF on 1.7% — so each scores 4 out of 10 after the error penalty. Cloudways DigitalOcean Standard (443 ms) and Cloudways DigitalOcean Premium (360 ms) were slower on average but served every request at a 0% error rate, each scoring 5 out of 10. The trade-off is clear: the Vultr and Linode plans are quicker per request but shed traffic at the ceiling, while the two DigitalOcean plans stay slower and complete the full load without dropping a request. Notable hosts in this test are WP Engine at an elite 27 ms, Hostinger Business at 31 ms, Kinsta at 40 ms, and SiteGround at 170 ms, all at 0% errors. Every Cloudways plan completed the test, and the two DigitalOcean plans cleared 100% of requests. Our method ramps 0 to 100 concurrent users over 60 seconds while measuring average response time and any dropped requests. The DigitalOcean Standard and Premium plans held 0% errors through peak load, so no visitor request is dropped during a traffic spike. The Vultr, Vultr HF, and Linode plans respond faster on completed requests but may drop 1.5% to 2.2% of requests right at the 100-user ceiling. Server Hardware Test Cloudways Vultr HF scored 7.6 out of 10 in the WPBenchmark test, which is competitive with managed hosts like Hostinger with 7.4 and Kinsta with 8.8. Even Cloudways Linode has a strong allocation with 7.2. However, Cloudways DO Premium scored 4.7 and DO Standard scored 4.7, indicating below average hardware allocation. Cloudways Vultr scored 4.3, indicating the lowest allocation among all Cloudways plans. WPBench measures allocated CPU, RAM and disk I/O independent of web server type. LiteSpeed and Apache will have no impact on the WPBench scores. A low WPBench score means the provider has limited resource allocation for the plan. The WPBench score difference between Cloudways Vultr HF ($16 per month) and Cloudways Vultr ($14 per month) is because of the NVMe storage and higher clock CPUs, which translate into better resource allocation. Cloudways Vultr HF with 7.6 or Cloudways Linode with 7.2 are the only plans that offer adequate compute for plugin heavy WordPress sites or WooCommerce stores. Global TTFB Cloudways DigitalOcean Standard recorded a cached global average of 386 ms across 40 locations, scoring 7 out of 10, tested without the Cloudflare Enterprise add-on. It averaged 178 ms in the Americas — 42 ms in Northern Virginia, 57 ms in Toronto, 124 ms in Dallas, and 218 ms in Los Angeles — with Latin America weaker at 386 ms in Santiago and 387 ms in São Paulo. Europe averaged 274 ms, strong for a US-origin host: 230 ms in London, 254 ms in Paris, 251 ms in Frankfurt, and 339 ms in Finland. Asia Pacific averaged 649 ms, clearly the weak region — 493 ms in Tokyo, 578 ms in Seoul, 629 ms in Sydney, 873 ms in Mumbai, and 879 ms in Delhi. Against the field, WP Engine leads at 65 ms with edge CDN, Hostinger Business records 351 ms with static CDN, Bluehost 224 ms with Cloudflare CDN, Cloudways 386 ms with no CDN, Kinsta 477 ms, and SiteGround 1,200 ms. Cloudways beats both Kinsta and SiteGround on global TTFB despite running without a CDN. Enabling the Cloudflare Enterprise add-on for $4.99 per month would sharply improve global delivery. While Cloudways global performance is adequate for US and European audiences, those targeting Asia Pacific can enable the Cloudflare Enterprise add-on or switch to WP Engine for faster delivery. The figures above reflect the DigitalOcean Standard plan; global TTFB tests for the Premium, Vultr, Vultr HF, and Linode plans are being added. Which Cloudways Plan Should You Pick? You can choose Bluehost if you want the highest raw server power with a WPbench of 9.6, budget pricing and can accept weekly backups and occasional load errors. For cleaner uptime, daily backups, and zero dropped requests under load, the Cloudways DigitalOcean Standard or Premium plan is the right choice, with no renewal surprise. Who Should Use Cloudways WordPress developers looking for server level control without managing raw infrastructure can choose Cloudways since the host provides SSH access, server scaling, staging environment with a 419 to 447 ms TTFB range and 99.99% uptime. Small business owners with target audiences in the US or Europe can use Cloudways as the host recorded an average of 178 ms in the Americas and 274 ms in Europe for $11 to $16 with no renewal surprises, which makes budgeting predictable. Users that need to migrate from shared hosting due to resource limitation can use Cloudways as the host offers cloud isolation and high scalability. Shared hosting users paying $8 to $18 per month at renewal are paying close to Cloudways prices but for a comparatively worse performance. WooCommerce stores that need reliable uptime and daily backups can use Cloudways. Further, such stores can benefit from Cloudways high scalability to scale up the resources during sale events. Users who are looking for multi CMS can also use Cloudways since the host supports WordPress, Magento, Laravel, and other PHP apps on the same server. Who Should NOT Use Cloudways Budget conscious beginners who need everything included for a nominal price should avoid Cloudways as the host requires you to buy addon like CDN for $4.99 per month and email hosting. This could take the total cost to $20 per month. On the contrary, Hostinger Business for just $3.69 per month includes static CDN, daily backups at a much lower cost than Cloudways. If your budget is under $10 per month, choosing a shared hosting is the practical way to go about it. If your site has heavy Asia Pacific traffic, Cloudways is not the ideal option for you since Cloudways Asia Pacific average is 649 ms without the CDN add-on, with TTFB as high as 873 ms in Mumbai and 879 ms in Delhi. The ideal hosts to choose in this case would be WP Engine with 246 ms in Asia Pacific or Hostinger Business with 287 ms, which should be measurably better for these audiences. Non technical users who want cPanel or Plesk should not use Cloudways as the host doesn’t come with any traditional file manager and users who rely on cPanel will find it hard with the steep learning curve of the Cloudways interface. Such users can go with SiteGround or Bluehost as both offer traditional panels. Users who need maximum server hardware at entry level should not use Cloudways as the host has WPBench score of 4.3 to 7.6 while Bluehost scored 9.6 and SiteGround scored 8.4, indicating more raw server allocation on their cheapest plans. Plugin heavy sites on a tight budget can go with shared hosts with a higher WPBench as this will deliver better compute per dollar. Our Verdict Cloudways DigitalOcean Standard scored 6.39 out of 10 in our 2026 rankings, the one Cloudways plan we currently score on a complete metric set. We recommend Cloudways for a managed cloud host with no renewal markup, uptime between 99.996% and 99.999% across all 5 plans, and strong US and European response times, provided you are comfortable managing email separately and adding a CDN for global reach. We do not recommend Cloudways if you are under a tight budget and your primary audience is in Asia or if you want a traditional cPanel interface. Across the 5 plans the choice is a trade-off: Cloudways Vultr HF ($16) and Linode ($14) carry the strongest hardware and fastest completed-request load times but drop 1.7% to 2.2% at peak load, while DigitalOcean Standard ($11) and Premium ($14) are slower but complete every request. If Cloudways is not the right fit, Hostinger Business is a strong alternative with a 351 ms global TTFB, static CDN, a $3.69 intro price, and a $7.99 renewal. This review is based on over 12,288,960 performance tests conducted across the 5 Cloudways plans between 2020 and May 2026 using tools such as Pingdom, Loader.io, SpeedVitals, and WPBenchmark. Methodology We purchase all hosting accounts with our own funds and none of these accounts is a promotional or press account. We purchased all 5 Cloudways plans separately and independently. Our testing tools comprise Pingdom for testing TTFB and uptime every 60 seconds for 24/7, Loader.io for load testing using 0 to 100 concurrent users over 60 seconds, SpeedVitals for measuring global TTFB from over 40 cities, and WPBenchmark to conduct 21 server hardware tests across 5 categories. We conduct over 525,600 tests per provider per year with tests conducted every minute, 24/7/365. We conducted over 2,628,000 Cloudways specific tests alone with 5 Cloudways plans per year. Our scoring method weights Performance at 80% — TTFB 22%, Uptime 22%, Load handling 18%, Global TTFB 13%, and Hardware 5% — and Value at 20% based on the intro price tier. Our data period is October 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026 for our current rankings. For this review, we referred to the historical data from 2020 for Cloudways DO Standard, 2021 for Cloudways Vultr, Cloudways Vultr HF, and Cloudways Linode, and 2022 for Cloudways DO Premium. Final Verdict: Is Cloudways Worth It for Beginners in 2026?
text: Choosing the right hosting provider can make or break your website. If your site is slow, crashes during traffic spikes, or feels complicated to manage, you’re not alone. Many beginners start with cheap shared hosting and later realize it’s holding them back. That’s where Cloudways enters the conversation. But the real question is: Is Cloudways actually worth it for beginners in 2026? Or is it better suited for developers and advanced users? In this honest review, we’ll cover: What Cloudways is How it works Performance test results Pros and cons Pricing breakdown Who should use it Who should avoid it Let’s dive in. What Is Cloudways? Cloudways is a managed cloud hosting platform that lets you host websites on top-tier cloud providers like: DigitalOcean Vultr Linode AWS Google Cloud Instead of dealing directly with complicated cloud infrastructure, Cloudways simplifies everything into an easy-to-use dashboard. Think of it as: Cloud power without cloud complexity. It removes the technical headaches while still giving you high performance and scalability. How Is Cloudways Different From Traditional Hosting? Most beginners start with shared hosting. Here’s the difference: Shared Hosting Hundreds of websites share one server Limited performance Cheap but overcrowded Slower during peak traffic Cloudways (Managed Cloud Hosting) Dedicated cloud resources Scalable servers Advanced caching Optimized for performance Pay for what you use With shared hosting, if another website on your server gets a traffic spike, your site slows down. With Cloudways, your resources are isolated. That’s a major advantage. Cloudways Performance Test (Real-World Results) Performance is where Cloudways stands out. For this review, we tested a basic WordPress installation on a DigitalOcean 1GB server. Results: Load time: 1.2 – 1.8 seconds Google PageSpeed score: 90+ (mobile) GTmetrix Grade: A Time to First Byte (TTFB): Under 200ms These are excellent numbers, especially without heavy optimization. Why is it fast? Because Cloudways includes: SSD-based servers Built-in advanced caching (Varnish, Redis) Optimized stack (Nginx + Apache hybrid) PHP 8.x support Optional Cloudflare CDN integration You don’t have to configure everything manually — most of it is pre-optimized. Is Cloudways Beginner-Friendly? This is where many people hesitate. Cloud hosting sounds technical. But Cloudways has made significant improvements in usability. What Beginners Will Like: ✔ Clean dashboard ✔ One-click WordPress installation ✔ Free SSL certificates ✔ Automated backups ✔ Staging environments ✔ Easy server scaling ✔ 24/7 live chat support You don’t need to use SSH or manage complex configurations. That said… It’s not as “plug-and-play” simple as Bluehost-style shared hosting. There is a slight learning curve if you’ve never used anything beyond cPanel. But most beginners adapt within a day or two. Cloudways Features Breakdown Let’s look at the core features. 1. One-Click App Installation You can install: WordPress WooCommerce Magento Laravel Joomla Custom PHP apps All within minutes. 2. Built-In Advanced Caching Cloudways includes: Varnish cache Redis object caching Memcached Breeze caching plugin (for WordPress) This reduces load times significantly compared to standard shared hosting. 3. Vertical Scaling Traffic spike? No problem. You can scale server resources in a few clicks without migrating your site. This is perfect for: Bloggers E-commerce stores Seasonal businesses Viral campaigns 4. Free SSL & Security Security features include: Free Let’s Encrypt SSL Dedicated firewall Regular security patches IP whitelisting Two-factor authentication Security setup is simple and beginner-friendly. 5. Automated Backups Daily backups are included. You can also: Set backup frequency Restore with one click This is extremely important for beginners who may accidentally break something. Cloudways Pricing (Is It Affordable?) Cloudways pricing depends on the cloud provider you choose. Here’s a general idea: DigitalOcean plans start around $11–$14/month Vultr similar pricing AWS and Google Cloud are more expensive Compared to shared hosting at $3/month, it seems higher. But you’re getting: Dedicated resources Cloud infrastructure Advanced caching Scalability When compared to premium managed hosts like Kinsta or WP Engine (which start at $30+ per month), Cloudways is very competitive . For beginners serious about growth, it’s reasonably priced. Pros and Cons of Cloudways Pros ✔ Excellent performance ✔ Scalable infrastructure ✔ No long-term contracts ✔ Multiple cloud provider options ✔ Strong security ✔ Good support ✔ Great for growing websites Cons ✘ No domain registration included ✘ No traditional email hosting (add-on required) ✘ Slight learning curve for absolute beginners ✘ Not as cheap as entry-level shared hosting It’s important to understand both sides before deciding. Who Should Use Cloudways? Cloudways is ideal for: Bloggers planning to grow Affiliate marketers Small businesses WooCommerce store owners Agencies managing client sites Anyone tired of slow shared hosting If your website generates income (or you plan it to), investing in performance makes sense. Who Should Avoid Cloudways? Cloudways may not be ideal if: You’re building your first test website You want the absolute cheapest hosting possible You need bundled email + domain + hosting in one place You’re uncomfortable learning a slightly new interface In that case, basic shared hosting may be enough – at least temporarily. Cloudways vs Shared Hosting: Final Comparison Feature Shared Hosting Cloudways Speed Moderate High Scalability Limited Easy scaling Resource Isolation No Yes Traffic Handling Weak Strong Price Cheap Mid-range Long-Term Growth Limited Excellent If you’re serious about performance and growth, Cloudways clearly wins . The Honest Verdict CreatorsRes rates Cloudways 9.1/10 — the strongest all-around bridge between cheap shared hosting and intimidating raw cloud infrastructure for freelancers, agencies, and growing WordPress teams in 2026. Spin up a server on DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS, or Google Cloud in a few clicks, and you get NVMe-backed performance, built-in caching, and a genuinely clean dashboard, without ever provisioning a droplet or SSH-ing into a box yourself. Cloudways has been owned by DigitalOcean since 2022, but continues to operate as its own product with independent multi-cloud support. Where Cloudways earns its 9.1 rather than a perfect score is the parts it deliberately leaves out. There's no cPanel for teams used to that interface, and email hosting isn't included, so you'll pair it with Rackspace email or another provider. For agencies and growing WordPress or Elementor sites that need real scalability and multi-cloud choice, that's a fair tradeoff, but it's worth knowing upfront if you expect an all-in-one shared-hosting-style package. Setting up on Cloudways feels less like renting hosting and more like configuring a cloud server through a translator that speaks plain English. You pick an app (WordPress, WooCommerce, Laravel, or a custom PHP stack), choose a cloud provider and server size, and within a few minutes you have a live server with caching, SSL, and backups already wired up, no terminal required unless you want one. Multi-Cloud Choice Pick DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS, or Google Cloud underneath the same Cloudways dashboard, and switch providers as your budget or region needs change. Configuring a cloud server in Cloudways: selecting infrastructure providers and adjusting compute resources without command-line setup. Lightning Stack & Object Cache Pro The newer NGINX-based Lightning Stack, plus built-in Varnish and Redis caching, keeps page loads snappy across every plan. Object Cache Pro, which usually runs $95/month standalone, now ships free on 4GB+ servers, and keeps database-heavy WordPress and WooCommerce sites fast under real load. Deploying WordPress on Cloudways: configuring the Nginx-based Lightning Stack and built-in caching engine directly during initial setup. 1-Click Staging & Cloning Spin up a staging copy of any site, test theme or plugin changes safely, then push live or clone the whole app to a new server in a couple of clicks. Team Collaboration & Git Integration Invite teammates with role-based permissions, deploy through Git integration, and manage multiple client servers from one unified account. The one honest catch Cloudways deliberately skips two things many hosts bundle in: there's no cPanel, so anyone married to that interface will need to adjust to Cloudways' own dashboard, and email hosting isn't included, so you'll add Rackspace email or another provider separately. For teams comfortable with a modern control panel and a separate inbox setup, neither is a dealbreaker, but both are worth planning for before you migrate. Start Cloudways Free Trial Today 5-day free trial • No credit card required to start Or read our full Kinsta review instead → Questions Beginners Ask Us Most Should I choose DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, or AWS on Cloudways? DigitalOcean is the best starting point for most sites thanks to its low entry price and consistent NVMe performance. Vultr and Linode are solid steps up for traffic spikes and broader data-center coverage, while AWS or Google Cloud make sense once you need enterprise-grade compliance, larger scale, or a specific data-center footprint. How well does Cloudways handle WordPress and Elementor sites? Cloudways runs WordPress and Elementor noticeably faster than typical shared hosting thanks to its NVMe-backed servers, built-in Redis and Varnish caching, and Object Cache Pro (free on 4GB+ servers), which keeps heavy Elementor page builders responsive even with large template libraries. Do I need to manage the server myself on Cloudways? No. Cloudways fully manages server provisioning, security patching, firewall configuration, and backups behind the scenes, so you get root-level cloud power through a simplified dashboard without touching the command line. How much does Cloudways cost per month? Cloudways starts at $11 per month for an entry-level DigitalOcean server with hourly or monthly billing, scaling up through higher-RAM tiers for larger stores and agencies, with no long-term contract required. Does Cloudways offer staging environments? Yes. Cloudways includes one-click staging environments and one-click cloning, letting you test theme changes, plugin updates, or Elementor edits safely before pushing them to a live production site. Does Cloudways include free SSL certificates? Yes. Cloudways provisions free, auto-renewing Let's Encrypt SSL certificates on every application with one click, and also supports custom or wildcard SSL certificates for agencies managing multiple domains. Is Cloudways worth it in 2026? Cloudways is worth it if you have outgrown shared hosting and want fast managed cloud servers without managing them yourself. Plans start at $11/month with hourly or monthly billing, and you get NVMe storage, built-in caching, staging and free SSL. If you need cPanel or bundled email, a traditional host is simpler. Is Cloudways good for blog hosting? Yes. Cloudways is a strong choice for WordPress blogs that get steady traffic, because its caching stack and NVMe servers keep pages fast and you can scale up RAM as the blog grows. For a brand-new blog with very little traffic, a $2–3/month shared host is cheaper to start with. Does Cloudways have a free trial? Yes. Cloudways offers a 5-day free trial on its Flexible plans and a 3-day free trial on Autonomous, and neither needs a credit card. You can launch a real server, install WordPress and test speed before you pay anything. What is Cloudways Autonomous? Cloudways Autonomous is a fully managed, auto-scaling WordPress plan where Cloudways handles servers, scaling and caching for you. It starts at $99/month for Growth, with Scale at $199 and Plus at $399, while Cloudways Flexible lets you pick and size your own cloud server from $11/month. Is Cloudways better than Kinsta or Hostinger? It depends on budget and control. Cloudways is cheaper than Kinsta, which starts at $35/month ($30/month billed annually), and gives you a choice of cloud providers. Hostinger is cheaper for beginners with intro shared plans around $3/month, but Cloudways delivers more server power and flexibility for growing sites. Who owns Cloudways? Cloudways has been owned by DigitalOcean since 2022. It still runs servers on several providers, including DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode (Akamai), AWS and Google Cloud, so you are not limited to DigitalOcean infrastructure.
